description: We are STARBOARD, where art and analysis navigate the universe together. Combining years of professional artistic experience, design expertise, and advanced data analysis, we transform complex space data into compelling visual stories. Our mission is to uncover the hidden narratives of space exploration, making science more engaging, accessible, and memorable through the fusion of creativity, technology, and research.
summary: School-age explorers discover the machines left on the Moon and Mars through three illustrated control rooms: Apollo 11, Viking 1 and Sojourner. They investigate NASA photographs, 3D models, real Viking weather and archive audio. “Where is it now?” and “Last Signal” explain what remains, why it was left behind and what it still teaches us. Guided quizzes reward discovery with personalized certificates.
details:
Spacecraft can stop transmitting while their contribution to science lives on. Abandoned, But Not Forgotten helps school-age children explore that legacy through three distinct, hand-drawn-style control rooms representing 1969, 1976 and 1997.

Each room combines a mission timeline, an interactive 3D viewer and a science investigation. Children explore original NASA photographs and source-linked exhibits, compare real Viking atmospheric pressure measurements, and listen to historical audio. Sojourner’s cassette presents four NASA/JPL podcast excerpts with transcripts.

“Where is it now?” connects NSSDCA catalog records with dated orbital photographs to explain the hardware’s location, condition and reasons for remaining. The ringing telephone opens “Last Signal”: a sourced modern narration about the mission’s ending, followed by a fading CRT screen. These stories are not presented as authentic final spacecraft transmissions. Uncertainty is preserved, including Eagle’s ascent-stage fate and Sojourner’s exact final parking location.

Three guided quiz questions earn a personalized mission certificate. Completing all three mission quizzes unlocks a combined award. Optional clues, illustrated guides and browser-saved progress support exploration without requiring an account.

We deliberately chose three missions for depth. Our distinguishing approach combines three illustrated historical environments, real archive evidence and connected activities that explain both the missions and the equipment left behind.

The team developed the concept, selected and checked sources, directed the visual style and reviewed the interactions. Enes Yasir ARICAN led software integration and technical coordination; Semih KARTAL led research and fact-checking; Görkem AYGEL led art direction and visual review; Emre ARICAN led usability and testing.

The application uses HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Three.js and local JSON records. It is in English and designed for landscape exploration.
